messages:
maria: Quick ping — PR 8124 (microbatch scheduler refactor) is passing CI but canary showed p95 +3.2% on the longseq workload. I attached the canary CSV to the gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf/8124-canary-summary

devin: can you paste the summary here? no external clicks during review pls :slightly_smiling_face:

maria: pasted below (numbers are p50/p95 tail in ms, canary vs baseline):
```
baseline longseq (seq=2048): p50 42.3 p95 380.1
canary (PR 8124): p50 43.0 p95 392.5  (+3.2% p95)
throughput stable within 1%
mem no regression
```

nora: thanks — that's small but tail increase is in canary only? did you run multiple seeds?

maria: ran 4 canaries across regions (us-west/us-east/eu) — this bump was consistent in 3/4, one run noisy but overlapping CI. p99 looks flat.

cal: what changed in scheduler? I skimmed the PR — looks like you changed the batch horizon heuristics and added a small wakeup jitter. Could that increase tail for very long sequences?

maria: correct. jitter to avoid head-of-line blocking when many small requests interleave with a long one. The tradeoff may slightly delay some long requests when horizon crosses the threshold. We tuned to keep latency SLO for mixed workloads.

devin: do we have per-sequence-length breakdown? if p95 increase concentrated on seq>1500 then it's expected and maybe acceptable for now.

maria: yes, seq buckets:
```
seq<256: p95 delta -0.8%
256-1024: p95 delta +0.4%
1025-2048: p95 delta +7.0%
```
so it's the long tail only.

nora: that's useful. For our SLOs we care about >2048 less; customers mostly hit <1024 but internal longseq tests exist. What's the canary traffic mix vs prod?

maria: canary used synthetic mix (60% small, 30% med, 10% long) — prod is more small-heavy (~85% <1024).

cal: given that, I'd be okay merging if we add a config knob to disable jitter for dedicated workloads that indicate high longseq usage and add a short rollout canary with 1% traffic and extra tail monitoring.

devin: agree. also add a small regression test in perf harness that runs a deterministic longseq microbench nightly. Then we can auto-detect regressions >5% and block.

maria: will update PR: add config flag (runtime.jitter.enabled) default true, add canary rollout plan and perf job. ETA EOD.

perf-bot: perf harness job queued: longseq-nightly-8124 (will report in ~30m) :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: note: if merged without rollout, ops will flag for rollback on any user-facing tail alerts. Recommend gating on canary-slo check.

nora: ok sounds like a plan. Devin/Nora => can we get approval after PR includes flag + perf job?

devin: will review the updated diff when posted. tentative +1 pending tests.

cal: +1 for the config knob approach, want to eyeball the canary rollout policy.

maria: updated the branch, pushed config and perf job, added short docs in the PR description with rollback steps and SLO checks. tagging for approvals.

devin: reviewed, left one nit about naming, but LGTM for merge gating.

nora: approved.

maria: thanks — will hold merge until perf-bot posts the nightly result and we confirm no >5% p95 delta on seq>1024. will update thread.

perf-bot: longseq-nightly-8124 completed: p95 delta for seq>1024 = +1.9% (within threshold). Full report: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/8124-canary

maria: perfect — merging in 10m. will run a 1% traffic canary and monitor. :rocket:
